entities.name: The Younger Lady
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
The Younger Lady is the informal appellation given to an unidentified royal female mummy, designated KV35YL, discovered in 1898 within tomb KV35 in Egypt's Valley of the Kings by archaeologist Victor Loret. This individual, whose remains are preserved at the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, holds immense significance for 18th Dynasty Egyptian history, particularly in clarifying the complex genealogies of the Amarna Period. Her identity as the biological mother of Pharaoh Tutankhamun and a daughter of Pharaoh Amenhotep III and his Great Royal Wife Tiye was conclusively established through DNA analysis conducted in 2010, resolving decades of speculation regarding Tutankhamun's immediate lineage.

The scientific identification of The Younger Lady's familial relationships provided critical insights into the royal succession following the reign of Akhenaten. The DNA evidence demonstrated her to be a full sister to Akhenaten, making Tutankhamun a child of incestuous union between two children of Amenhotep III and Tiye. This discovery not only pinpointed Tutankhamun's direct maternal ancestor but also illuminated the intricate and often consanguineous marital practices within the New Kingdom pharaonic elite, particularly during a period of significant religious and political upheaval.

The revelation of The Younger Lady's identity profoundly impacted our understanding of the Amarna royal family, providing concrete genetic evidence that corroborated and, in some cases, reshaped historical theories based on inscriptions and iconography. Her genetic profile links key figures of the late 18th Dynasty, serving as a crucial anchor for reconstructing the dynastic tree and understanding the health implications of royal intermarriage. This breakthrough underscored the power of modern forensic archaeology to unlock ancient secrets, transforming a nameless mummy into a vital historical witness.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The identification of The Younger Lady provided definitive answers to the long-debated parentage of Pharaoh Tutankhamun and clarified critical genealogies of the 18th Dynasty Amarna Period, significantly enhancing understanding of this pivotal era in ancient Egyptian history.
